html:
The Berbers, or Amazigh, are the native peoples of North Africa west of Egypt, from the Atlantic coast of Morocco to the oases of the western desert, and south into the Sahara. On the map they hold this land from 1500 to 700 BCE, and again in 900 CE in the western Sahara.

Their ancestors include the herders of the green Sahara, the Saharan pastoral nomads. Egyptian records call the Berbers' ancestors Libyans and show them as raiders and later as soldiers and even pharaohs of Egypt.

They met many outsiders. Phoenicians and then Carthage traded on the coast, and Berber kingdoms rose behind it, such as Numidia and Mauretania, which later fell under Rome. The Arab conquests of the late 600s brought Islam. Berber armies then helped conquer Spain, and Berber movements founded great states of their own, the Almoravids and Almohads. In the desert, the Tuareg kept the old Tifinagh script. Today tens of millions speak Berber languages in Morocco and Algeria.
